{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Richard F. Johnsonbaugh''' (born 1941)<ref>[http://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n80140478.html Library of congress catalog entry], retrieved 2019-04-11.</ref> is an American [[mathematician]] and [[computer scientist]].  His interests include [[discrete mathematics]] and the [[history of mathematics]]. He is the author of several textbooks.

Johnsonbaugh earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Yale University]], and then moved to the [[University of Oregon]] for graduate study.<ref name=authorbio>Author biography from ''Discrete Mathematics'' (8th ed.)</ref> He completed his Ph.D. at Oregon in 1969. His dissertation, ''I. Classical Fundamental Groups and Covering Space Theory in the Setting of Cartan and Chevalley; II. Spaces and Algebras of Vector-Valued Differentiable Functions'', was supervised by Bertram Yood.<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=12493}}</ref> He also has a second master's degree in computer science from the [[University of Illinois at Chicago]].<ref name=authorbio/>

He is currently [[professor emeritus]] at [[De Paul University]].<ref name=authorbio/>

==Books==
*''Discrete Mathematics'' (MacMillan, 1984; 8th ed., Pearson, 2018)<ref>Review of ''Discrete Mathematics'':
*Charles F. Kelemen (1987), ''American Mathematical Monthly'', {{JSTOR|2322865}}, {{doi|10.2307/2322865}}</ref>
*''Foundations of Mathematical Analysis'' (with W. E. Pfaffenberger, Marcel Dekker, 1981; Dover, 2010)<ref>Reviews of ''Foundations of Mathematical Analysis'':
*William Eames (1982), ''Mathematical Reviews'', {{MR|0599741}}
*Wilfred Kaplan (1984), ''American Mathematical Monthly'', {{JSTOR| 2975675}}, {{doi|10.2307/2975675}}
*H. Ahrens (1986), ''Biometrical Journal'', {{doi|10.1002/bimj.4710280112}}</ref>
*''Applications Programming in ANSI C'' (with Martin Kalin, Prentice Hall, 1993; 3rd ed., 1996)
*''Object-oriented Programming in C++'' (with Martin Kalin, Prentice Hall, 1995)
*''Algorithms'' (with Marcus Schaefer, Prentice Hall, 2003)<ref>Review of ''Algorithms'':
*Dean Kelley (2009), ''SIGACT News'', {{doi|10.1145/1556154.1556159}}</ref>
